title: Application of a deep learning-based system for eyelid margin signs identification training and testing in dry eye disease education.
summary: The controlled study compared 40 medical students randomized to conventional learning or a deep-learning platform with real-time eyelid-margin feedback. After two weeks, the platform group had a higher total assessment score (56.95 ± 5.95 vs 53.37 ± 4.32, p=0.035) and greater accuracy for identifying meibomian-gland-orifice plugging (77.6% vs 67.4%, p=0.021).
ai_technology: A deep-learning system provides interactive identification and real-time feedback on abnormal eyelid-margin signs during dry-eye assessment training.
organization: Peking University Third Hospital; Peking University Health Science Center

evidence.tested: In a randomized study of 40 medical students, the deep-learning feedback platform group scored 56.95 ± 5.95 versus 53.37 ± 4.32 after training (p=0.035); accuracy for identifying meibomian-gland-orifice plugging was 77.6% versus 67.4% (p=0.021). This small educational study does not establish clinical benefit.
evidence.unknown: Independent replication and prospective real-world benefit are not established in the reviewed study.
evidence.ai_role: A deep-learning system provides interactive identification and real-time feedback on abnormal eyelid-margin signs during dry-eye assessment training.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
